the regularized autoencoder, with a proper contractive penalty and a proper reconstruction loss, can be used to estimate a density function.
, in the large data regime, the regularized auto encoder implicitly learns the true density function of the data, and the training procedure is equivalent to a MLE procedure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide the first general mathematical framework for denoising and/or contractive autoencoder to be used as generative models, with a clear connection to the data generating process and the training procedure, for both continuous and discrete variables.

we provide a new framework for training denoising auto-encoders, which is able to learn the underlying data generating probability distribution in a principled way, while handling discrete and continuous valued data.
we propose a new framework for training regularized autoencoders as generative models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

regularized auto encodes are in fact generative models, and can be seen as a particular form of energy based model, where the energy function is a sum of a contractive penalty and a reconstruction error.

regularized autoencoders can be seen as a particular case of a much more general family of algorithms, called generalized denoising autoencoders (GDAEs), which can be used for sampling from a wide variety of distributions.
the training procedure of a denoising autoencoder can be seen as an instance of maximum likelihood estimation for a generative model.
